40:      "summary": "Albanese and abelian-variety leg. Three of five children done (.ab, .codim1, .rationalmaps);
.symmetric and .universal remain, and BOTH are blocked on the same single object.

STATE AT RUN 0069 r5, measured not estimated:
 * Milne III.6.1 (the Albanese universal property) is PROVED over the symmetric power taken
   as an interface -- Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean, sorry-free, both directions.
 * Milne Lemma 3.3 (pure codim-1 indeterminacy into a group variety) is PROVED, and with it
   Thm 3.2's rational-map extension is unconditional. CodimOneExtension.lean and
   RigidityLemma.lean are at ZERO sorries -- any brief or note citing sorries there is
   quoting docstring prose.
 * ALL SIX remaining sorries in the leg are in Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean, and every one is
   stated against SymmetricPower, a sorry-BODIED definition. They are undischargeable as
   stated, not merely unproved: an equation between morphisms out of a junk term carries no
   information. albanese_universal_property reports sorryAx and must not be called landed.

THE ONE MISSING OBJECT is Sym^g C for the proper curve, equivalently the instance
HasColimit (permDiagram C g) in Over (Spec kbar) -- proved EQUIVALENT to the datum the
Albanese theorems consume (SymPowColimit.hasColimit_permDiagram_iff), so the reduction is
lossless. Over.forget creates colimits, so no over-category bookkeeping is needed: it is a
statement about Scheme.

THE AFFINE HALF IS NOW DONE, with its carrier named and over the base: SymPowTensorAction
.lean (the S_n-action on the n-fold tensor power of a RING -- mathlib had permutation only as
a linear equiv, so Milne's carrier was not even STATEABLE) and SymPowInvariantsUnder.lean
(the invariants ARE the limit in Under k, dually a colimit in (Under k)^op).

WHAT REMAINS IS THE GLUING, and it is now three named inputs rather than an unsized
subproject. One of the three closed this round: StableAffineCoverGroup.lean proves every
point has a G-STABLE affine open neighbourhood for a bare finite group -- the same proof as
Picard/StableAffineCover.lean, whose Galois binder its body never touches. The other two:
(i) cocycle/overlap agreement of the affine chart quotients; (ii) OrbitsInAffineOpen for the
curve, which is where quasi-projectivity enters and mathlib has no quasi-projectivity
vocabulary at this pin.

Availability measured at this pin so nobody re-searches: HasCoproducts Scheme YES,
HasCoequalizers/HasPushouts Scheme NO, Scheme.GlueData YES.

DELTA, run 0069 r7 (nothing above is retracted; the sorry count is UNCHANGED at six).
The affine half of the symmetric-power route closed out. Item 3 of the four-item glue-data
bill is DONE (Albanese/TensorPowerCofan.lean packages the tensor power as the n-ary coproduct
in Under k), so the bill is 3 SUPPLIED / 1 OPEN, and the affine carrier is now NAMED at both
ends: SymPowAffineCarrier.tensorPowerOpIsoPiObj (the n-fold product permDiagram is built on IS
op of the tensor power, actions matched) and SymPowAffineQuotient.colimitPermDiagramIsoFixed
(the colimit IS op of Milne's (A^{⊗n})^{S_n}). SymPowColimit §5's bold caveat "the carrier is
not named in Lean" is discharged and deleted. 12 new declarations, all kernel-checked EXIT=0
and axiom-clean with controls firing sorryAx.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated because "3 of 4" invites the wrong inference: item 4 -- the
overlap/cocycle agreement of the chart quotients and OrbitsInAffineOpen FOR THE CURVE -- is
the whole of the geometry, and it is untouched. The affine chain is stated over mkUnder k A in
(Under k)-op; C is a proper curve in Over (Spec kbar). Nothing in AlbaneseUP /
AlbaneseFromData / AlbaneseFromColimit mentions any of the new names (checked, zero hits), so
this is integration WITHIN the affine story, not with the capstone. Also unbuilt: the second
bridge of Milne's affine half, that (Under k)-op IS affine k-schemes -- so all of it is
k-algebra language rather than Spec-language.

TWO SELF-CORRECTIONS worth more than the lemmas, both caught before or by the kernel:
 (a) I first offered an EXISTENCE restatement as the carrier-naming payoff. Vacuous: it was
     literally symPowData_affineAlgebra instantiated, and which proof supplied the instance is
     invisible in it. Then I measured the instance -- infer_instance discharges the HasColimit
     from cocompleteness alone -- so that theorem adds nothing provable either. Naming an
     object requires a statement that MENTIONS the object.
 (b) My first header said the "carrier is not named" caveat was "now false" on the strength of
     naming the INPUT (the object the action acts on) when the caveat is about the QUOTIENT.
     Input vs output. Repaired, then the quotient actually proved, then the caveat deleted.",
92:      "summary": "Extend rational maps across codimension one. SORRY-FREE (run 0069, commit 8a5dc2a66).

Milne Lemma 3.3 (indeterminacy_pure_codim_one_into_grpScheme, Albanese/Milne33.lean) is proved and axiom-clean, so Z(f) = empty for group-variety targets and extend_to_av (Milne Theorem 3.2) is unconditional. Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean carries no sorry.

It lives DOWNSTREAM of CodimOneExtension.lean rather than in it: the difference-map / pole-purity / Hauptidealsatz-transport layers (Albanese/Milne33{Rows,Diagonal,RowSection,Pullback,CMEquidim,KernelGen,Transport,TransportLocal}.lean) import that file, so stating the keystone there is an import cycle. Ported sorry-free from the sibling Rebuild tree, which had developed the chain on the identical toolchain and mathlib pin; every algebra prerequisite already existed in AJC. Route and both implementation notes are on hgraph node ca0776c343e5.

Caveat on the axiom claim: extend_to_av is unconditional GIVEN an abelian variety. A fresh-context review found no axiom-clean inhabitant of the AV instance package in this development today (a synthesis site at A := Jacobian C reports sorryAx, via the Picard seam upstream). That is not a defect in this leg, but the two claims are different.

RE-MEASURED run 0069 r7, because the ajc-albanese task brief handed to that session listed five
sorry line numbers in CodimOneExtension.lean (:216, :218, :752, :1402, :1751) and three in
RigidityLemma.lean (:481, :673, :764), and flagged Milne 3.3 as the highest-leverage OPEN node.
All of that is stale: those line numbers land in DOCSTRING PROSE, both files carry zero code
sorries, and #print axioms on the lock-free scratch root gives
[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] for every one of

  Scheme.RationalMap.CodimOneFree, Scheme.gammaSpecField_ringEquiv,
  Scheme.localRing_dvr_of_codim_one, Scheme.RationalMap.indeterminacy_pure_codim_one_into_grpScheme,
  Scheme.RationalMap.extend_to_av, rigidity_core.

So this row's `done` is correct and the brief is what needs fixing (recorded as inbox I-0732).
The caveat above about the AV instance package still stands unchanged -- it is about inhabiting
the abelian-variety hypotheses at A := Jacobian C, which is the Picard seam, not this leg.",

is PROVED (Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean, axiom-clean); the residue is the OBJECT
Sym^g C, equivalently the single instance HasColimit (permDiagram C g)
(SymPowColimit.hasColimit_permDiagram_iff -- an equivalence, so the reduction is lossless).

Route: explicit Scheme.GlueData from affine charts. The bill is four items. As of run 0069 r7:
3 SUPPLIED, 1 OPEN. The authoritative count lives in StableAffineCoverGroup.lean's header --
this row is a pointer to it, not a second source of truth (a review found the two disagreeing).
Read the change from r6's "2 supplied, 1 partial, 1 open" as item 3 completing, NOT as
vindicating an older row that said "3 of 4" for a different and wrong reason.

 1. DONE. G-stable affine open neighbourhoods for a finite group acting by automorphisms
    (Albanese/StableAffineCoverGroup.lean) plus exists_stable_affineOpen_perm{,_over}.
 2. DONE. The Aut-valued S_n-action MonObj.permAutHom (Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean).
 3. DONE (r7). Algebra level: TensorPowerCoproduct.lean (existsUnique_coprodLift,
    coprodLift_permAlgHom, permAlgHom_comp_singleAlgHom). The Cofan/IsColimit packaging that
    was the missing half: TensorPowerCofan.lean (tensorPowerCofanIsColimit, plus
    tensorPowerFanIsLimit for the (Under k)-op variance and tensorPowerCofan_inj_permAlgHom
    for equivariance on the coprojections). The one trap, measured: CommRingCat.toAlgHom is
    typed over the algebra instance REBUILT from the structure morphism, not the ambient one,
    so it does not unify -- algHomOfMkUnderHom is the version over the ambient instance
    (proof: Under.w plus a congrArg; both round trips rfl).
 4. OPEN, and genuinely geometric: the overlap/cocycle agreement of the chart quotients, and
    OrbitsInAffineOpen FOR THE CURVE -- where quasi-projectivity enters and mathlib has no
    such vocabulary at this pin. THIS IS THE WHOLE REMAINING RESIDUE of the affine-and-glue
    route.

BEYOND THE BILL, r7 also named the affine carrier, which three files had recorded as expected
but unproved:
 * SymPowAffineCarrier.tensorPowerOpIsoPiObj -- the n-fold product in (Under k)-op that
   permDiagram is BUILT ON is op (mkUnder k (tensor power)), i.e. (Spec_k A)^n = Spec_k A^{⊗n},
   with permAut_eq_op_permAlgHom matching the actions (and it carries e-inverse; the kernel
   forced that -- the wrong variance leaves a goal true only at an involution).
 * SymPowAffineQuotient.colimitPermDiagramIsoFixed -- the QUOTIENT:
   colimit (permDiagram (op (mkUnder k A)) n) is iso to op (fixedUnder ... (tensor power)),
   Milne III.3 Prop 3.1's affine half with the object identified. SymPowColimit §5's bold
   caveat "the carrier is not named in Lean" is discharged and deleted.

TWO HONEST LIMITS ON THAT, both measured this round rather than assumed:
 (a) The accompanying HasColimit (permDiagram (op (mkUnder k A)) n) is NOT a new fact --
     infer_instance discharges it from cocompleteness. Only the ISO is new. An earlier draft
     offered an existence restatement as the payoff; it was vacuous, because naming an object
     needs a statement that MENTIONS the object.
 (b) The SECOND bridge of Milne's affine half -- that (Under k)-op IS the category of affine
     k-schemes, via Over.opEquivOpUnder and AffineScheme.equivCommRingCat -- is still unbuilt.
     So all of the above is k-ALGEBRA language, not Spec-language, and symPowData_affineAlgebra
     was not rewritten to consume the named carrier.

CONSUMPTION, checked by grep not asserted: SymPowAffineCarrier.lean consumes the Cofan layer in
proof bodies (:138, :150, :184) and SymPowAffineQuotient consumes that -- the first consumer of
anything this lane has built in five rounds. But AlbaneseUP / AlbaneseFromData /
AlbaneseFromColimit mention NONE of these names (zero hits). This is a consumer inside the
affine story, not integration with the capstone; item 4 is what stands between.

AlbaneseUP.lean's six sorries are UNCHANGED and albanese_universal_property still reports
sorryAx. All six are stated against the sorry-BODIED SymmetricPower, so they remain
undischargeable as stated rather than merely unproved.
",
171:      "summary": "Albanese universal property. THE ARGUMENT IS PROVED (run 0069); what remains is one precisely-named typeclass instance, not "one missing object" in general.

MILNE III.6.1 IS PROVED, both connector directions, over the symmetric power taken as an interface rather than a sorry -- Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean and Albanese/AlbaneseJacobian.lean, sorry-free. Forward (symAVMap_eq_of_albanese_eq) needs psi to be a HOMOMORPHISM: pushing psi through the g-fold sum is map_prod (IsMonHom.monoidHom), exactly where Milne's step 5 uses homomorphy. Backward (albanese_eq_of_symAVMap_eq) needs neither that nor the quotient universal property -- it is restriction along Q |-> (Q,P0,...,P0) plus the collapse basePointShift_comp_powSum.

THE RESIDUE IS NOW PRECISE (Albanese/AlbaneseFromColimit.lean, corrected 2026-07-28 commit af3d7b6a2 after an earlier draft got the binder wrong): exists_unique_albanese_of_scheme_colimits takes no SymPowData argument and no hproj argument -- the symmetric power is symPowOfColimit C g and its symmetry is colimit.w, free at every n. The single remaining typeclass hypothesis is HasColimit (permDiagram C g): ONE diagram, for THIS curve and THIS g, in Over (Spec kbar). It is NOT HasColimitsOfShape (SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin g))) Scheme -- that shape-quantified form is strictly stronger, is not what hasColimit_permDiagram_iff covers, and is believed FALSE at this pin (schemes have no coequalizers in general); a theorem carrying it would be vacuous. See AJC.albanese.symmetric for the state of discharging that instance. UPDATED run 0069 r7: this row previously said "TWO residues now, in order: the Cofan/IsColimit packaging in (Under k)-op ... and then the gluing". The FIRST is closed (Albanese/TensorPowerCofan.lean), so there is ONE residue left and it is the geometric wall: the gluing/cocycle compatibility of the chart quotients plus OrbitsInAffineOpen for the curve, where quasi-projectivity enters and mathlib has no such vocabulary at this pin. r7 also named the affine carrier at both ends (SymPowAffineCarrier.tensorPowerOpIsoPiObj for the input, SymPowAffineQuotient.colimitPermDiagramIsoFixed for the quotient = Milne III.3 Prop 3.1's affine half with the object identified), which discharged SymPowColimit §5's "carrier is not named in Lean" caveat. NONE of that shortens the curve residue: the affine chain is stated over mkUnder k A in (Under k)-op, and C is a proper curve in Over (Spec kbar). Do not read "3 of 4 items supplied" as "3/4 of the way to Sym^g C" -- item 4 is the whole of the geometry.

THE MEASUREMENT, which attributes the residual sorry rather than asserting whose it is:
    #print axioms exists_unique_albanese_of_scheme_colimits -> [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]  AXIOM-CLEAN
    #print axioms Pic0.albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData    -> [propext, sorryAx, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
Same statement; the sole difference is whether the target group object is Pic0.jacobianScheme C or an arbitrary abelian variety. So the entire sorryAx residue of the Pic0 form is the PICARD REPRESENTABILITY SEAM upstream of this leg, and none of it is Milne's argument.

DISCHARGED UNCONDITIONALLY (Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean, on the project's four-instance abelian-variety package): commutativity of an abelian variety (Milne I.1.4) and pointed rigidity (Milne I.1.2). The obstruction had been instance KEYING through the monoidal notation, not missing mathematics.

REMAINING INPUTS: (1) HasColimit (permDiagram C g) -- see AJC.albanese.symmetric; (2) Milne III.5.1(a) birationality as a SECTION of f^(g) over a dense open. The descent around them is closed: extend_to_av (Milne Thm 3.2) is unconditional and axiom-clean, and exists_unique_descent_of_section / hom_ext_of_dense_open package it in elementary terms with no rational map in the statement.

NOT A CLOSED RESULT ABOUT THE JACOBIAN, and the module headers say so in those words. The pinned Pic0.albanese_universal_property still reports sorryAx and its six sorries in AlbaneseUP.lean are UNCHANGED -- they are stated against a sorry-BODIED SymmetricPower and are undischargeable as stated, which the AlbaneseUP.lean header now records along with a pointer to where the mathematics lives.
",
675:      "summary": "Thirteen bounded prose and truth passes. The route-of-record work is complete in the sense that matters: the blueprint no longer presents the Quot endgame as the live route AND the committed Milne-Kollar route now has its own section with landed mathematics in it rather than only a description.  NEW (run 0054): FGA chapter sec:fga_pic_milne_kollar, five nodes with complete proofs and resolving Lean pins -- thm:rigid_pushforward_locally_free over lem:p1_integral (the rigidified pushforward and the integrality of P^1 under it), thm:speiser_descent, thm:galois_quotient_points, lem:stable_affine_open (the finite Galois quotient), plus rem:orbit_in_affine_hypothesis. That remark states what the route comparison had been leaving implicit: BOTH routes need a hypothesis the Hironaka example fails, and the difference is availability, not hypothesis-freeness. The dependency section gives each route its own input list, and Jacobian.tex's Albanese leaf is split so the algebraically closed case carries its proof (lem:pic0_isAlbanese_algClosed).  Measured on the current tree (2026-07-27): 623-page LuaLaTeX PDF, ZERO errors, ZERO unresolved references, zero multiply-defined labels. Two pre-existing LaTeX breakages fixed in Picard_GrassmannianCells.tex -- an unbraced ] closing an amsthm optional argument early, twice, which made the first pass die and only produced a PDF because a second pass ran past it. The third node carries its chi-ledger hypothesis IN the statement rather than in a remark, because degree_principal_eq_zero_of_isAlgClosed_curve measures axiom-clean while remaining conditional; pinning it as unconditional would have been the exact defect the issue was filed to prevent. The trap-(b) reading went on the hgraph node as a comment, not into the .tex. Sync after: 1933 blueprint nodes, 4629 lean nodes, zero pin warnings, both new pins lean_ok. That was wrong -- re-measured against both blueprint entry points (web.tex and print.tex), sync still reports exactly 33 \lean{} pins naming declarations absent from the Lean sources. Seven of the 33 are deliberate AlgebraicGeometry.TODO.* placeholders (Quot-lane and etale-sheafification forward references); the remaining 26 are pins to names that were renamed or never written, concentrated in the Cohomology pushforward/tilde lanes and the section-graded-ring lane. None of the 33 is one of this session's five new nodes, all of which resolve. Remaining printable debt: 747 overfull boxes. AJC.maintenance.blueprint.pins.remaining-contracts is where this work belongs.

NEW (run 0054 s0010) -- the route-of-record work is now complete on BOTH sides, which it was not before. The FGA chapter had described the two routes correctly for a while, but four Quot-lane chapters still described the quotient endgame in the PRESENT TENSE as how the Picard scheme gets built. Nine passages re-aimed across Picard_QuotScheme, Picard_FlatteningStratification, Picard_LineBundleCoherence and Picard_SectionGradedRing (details on the .prose child); no mathematics deleted, no statement weakened, no annotation touched. Flattening stratification in particular now states its theorem independent of any moduli construction and then records who consumes it, rather than presenting itself as a step inside Quot.

Jacobian.tex gains three nodes for leaf A: lem:curve_rational_point_algClosed (leanok, complete proof -- Jacobian space gives a closed point, and over k = k-bar a closed point is a section), rem:rational_point_scope (which of the headline's five obligations is FALSE and which four are merely unproved -- a distinction no axiom check can make), and def:picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed. Two of the 33 are a TOOLING false negative -- the graph's Lean indexer does not accept a declaration whose name carries a universe-binder suffix (theorem foo.{u,v}); those two declarations exist and are axiom-clean, their nodes now correctly carry leanok, and the warnings will persist until I-0452 is fixed upstream.

1503:      "summary": "Headline obligation 5: isAlbanese_pic0Et (Jacobian.lean:660, bare sorry) -- the Albanese universal property of Pic0SchemeEt over an ARBITRARY field. ADVANCED in its SUPPLY ROUTE, obligation UNTOUCHED, by ajc-p4 (run 0086 r4). Owner released.

*** THE r2 COSTING ON THIS ROW WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND IS RETRACTED (I-1285, my own item I-1115). Read this before pricing anything here. ***

WHAT r2 PUBLISHED: the leg's IsAlgClosed is load-bearing at exactly ONE lemma, Milne 3.1's regularity input (isRegularLocalRing_localizationAtPrime_of_isStandardSmooth_of_isAlgClosed, CodimOneExtension.lean:806), which "needs a residue-degree-aware version, not a binder deletion"; and Milne 3.3 has NO IsAlgClosed in either project.

(1) THE NAMED LEMMA IS NOT THE ONE THE CHAIN CALLS. isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_smooth (:1237) delegates to isRegularLocalRing_of_isLocalization_atPrime_of_isStandardSmooth_of_perfectField (Albanese/SmoothPrimeRegularity.lean:665) -- sorry-free, ARBITRARY prime, PERFECT field -- and says so in its own docstring. Plus Albanese/CodimOnePerfectFieldWitness.lean, 6 declarations, 0 sorries: NON-VACUITY BY INSTANTIATION at P^1 over Q and over F_5, with every binder discharged by synthesis from the p1Over stack -- so the weakened binder is not forced closed again by the remaining ones. (2) THE LIVE LINK IS MILNE 3.3, ONE HOP ABOVE WHERE r2 PUT IT. indeterminacy_pure_codim_one_into_grpScheme binds [IsAlgClosed] on the section VARIABLE line (Milne33.lean:57) -- invisible in the declaration header, visible to #check, which is how r2 came to report it absent. Only 3 of the 12 modules in that cone carry the binder; the other two are the closed-point layers.

SO THE REMAINING DISTANCE ON THE SUPPLY ROUTE, corrected: Milne 3.3's closed-point row argument, and NOTHING ELSE in the Milne section I.3 chain. A lane must replace the row argument's k-rational-point construction at closed points by something that survives a residue field strictly larger than k -- not weaken a binder.

NOT PROGRESS ON THE SORRY, stated plainly: isAlbanese_pic0Et is UNTOUCHED, no antecedent is witnessed at any curve, and PerfectField is not Field -- the imperfect case (F_p(t)) is outside all five theorems (measured: PerfectField (RatFunc (ZMod 5)) does not hold). The other residues from r2 stand unchanged: Sym^g C i.e. HasColimit (permDiagram C g) -- see AJC.albanese.symmetric -- the descent datum uniformly in the target, genus 0 (Mumford section 4), the basepoint condition, and the Abel-Jacobi transport to Pic0SchemeEt.",
1663:      "summary": "r2 CORRECTION TO THIS NODE'S OWN BREAK ANALYSIS (pic-e, run 0095, 2026-07-30): G1 IS NO LONGER PART OF THE BREAK. The seam sorry fgaPicardRepresentability is untouched and no antecedent of it is witnessed for any curve.

The paragraph below says "the break is exactly where the field returns to k: G1/G3, and G4 downstream". G1 is now OFF that list, and not because it was re-scoped -- because its remaining debt is a theorem. isInvariantMatch_canonical (Picard/PicEtInvariantMatch.lean, 8881ebccad + 3eedc3c923, rooted, zero sorries, lake build 8696 jobs EXIT=0, axiom-clean against the seam firing sorryAx) discharges the G1 predicate match at the canonical Galois action, for every test, with NO hypothesis beyond the k'-side representation and the curve's own binders: arbitrary k, arbitrary k'/k, no finiteness, no separability, no IsGalois, no condition on Gal(k'/k). Full printed signature checked per I-1292.

It is free because the canonical action's gamma-component IS twistMor gamma, which is DEFINED by transporting the functor action galoisActionPicEt along the representation -- so equivariance and invariance are two readings of one equation, and naturality converts between them. Nobody had asked what the action was defined as; four rows priced a match against it as though it were arbitrary.

SO THE RESTATED-G3 DESCENT ROUTE THIS NODE CALLS "THE REPAIR" NOW HAS TWO NAMED ANTECEDENTS BETWEEN A k'-SIDE REPRESENTATION AND CLAUSE (1) FIELD 1, not four: the Galois quotient at a glued non-affine X' (pic-f, confirmed building at the canonical-action shape) and hcov (AJC.picrep.etale-rep.hcov, owned by pic-a whose run has since ended -- see I-1567 before taking it). Consumers should call seamClauseOne_of_isGaloisQuotient_noMatch.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, and it is the whole of what remains: k'-side representability itself. That is the campaign's undischarged output and still has nothing behind it, so "what survives of the pessimism" below stands verbatim. Removing G1 shortens the list between rep and clause (1); it does not move rep.

    11	
    12	The group-object interface for schemes supplies canonical translations between
    13	sections.  Proper geometrically integral group schemes over a field are
    14	commutative, giving the categorical core of Milne's abelian-variety language.
    15	-/

    30	  {G : C} [GrpObj G] {X : C}
    31	
    32	/- The cartesian identity used when reducing the geometric rigidity lemma to
    33	   its projection/slice equation. -/
    34	theorem rigidity_snd_lift
    35	    {X Y : C} (x₀ : 𝟙_ C ⟶ X) :
    36	    snd X Y ≫ lift (toUnit Y ≫ x₀) (𝟙 Y) =
    37	      lift (toUnit (X ⊗ Y) ≫ x₀) (snd X Y) := by
    38	  ext1 <;> simp
    39	
    40	/- Invariance under replacing the first coordinate by `x₀` is equivalent to
    41	   factoring through the second projection. -/
    42	theorem factors_through_snd_iff
    43	    {X Y Z : C} (x₀ : 𝟙_ C ⟶ X) (f : X ⊗ Y ⟶ Z) :
    44	    (∃ g : Y ⟶ Z, f = snd X Y ≫ g) ↔
    45	      lift (toUnit (X ⊗ Y) ≫ x₀) (snd X Y) ≫ f = f := by
    46	  constructor
    47	  · rintro ⟨g, rfl⟩
    48	    rw [← rigidity_snd_lift x₀]
    49	    simp
    50	  · intro h
    51	    refine ⟨lift (toUnit Y ≫ x₀) (𝟙 Y) ≫ f, ?_⟩
    52	    calc
    53	      f = lift (toUnit (X ⊗ Y) ≫ x₀) (snd X Y) ≫ f := h.symm
    54	      _ = (snd X Y ≫ lift (toUnit Y ≫ x₀) (𝟙 Y)) ≫ f := by
    55	        rw [rigidity_snd_lift x₀]
    56	      _ = snd X Y ≫ (lift (toUnit Y ≫ x₀) (𝟙 Y) ≫ f) :=
    57	        Category.assoc _ _ _
    58	
    59	/- The factor through the second projection is unique.  This is the
    60	   categorical cancellation step used when the rigidity slice is evaluated
    61	   at the distinguished first-coordinate section. -/
    62	theorem factor_through_snd_unique
    63	    {X Y Z : C} (x₀ : 𝟙_ C ⟶ X) (f : X ⊗ Y ⟶ Z)
    64	    {g₁ g₂ : Y ⟶ Z} (h₁ : f = snd X Y ≫ g₁)
    65	    (h₂ : f = snd X Y ≫ g₂) : g₁ = g₂ := by
    66	  have h := congrArg (fun q => lift (toUnit Y ≫ x₀) (𝟙 Y) ≫ q)
    67	    (h₁.symm.trans h₂)
    68	  simpa using h
    69	
    70	/- The rigidity factorization can be stated with a unique factor. -/
    71	theorem existsUnique_factor_through_snd_iff
    72	    {X Y Z : C} (x₀ : 𝟙_ C ⟶ X) (f : X ⊗ Y ⟶ Z) :
    73	    (∃! g : Y ⟶ Z, f = snd X Y ≫ g) ↔
    74	      lift (toUnit (X ⊗ Y) ≫ x₀) (snd X Y) ≫ f = f := by
    75	  constructor
    76	  · rintro ⟨g, hg, _⟩
    77	    exact (factors_through_snd_iff x₀ f).mp ⟨g, hg⟩
    78	  · intro h
    79	    have hex : ∃ g : Y ⟶ Z, f = snd X Y ≫ g :=
    80	      (factors_through_snd_iff x₀ f).mpr h
    81	    obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := hex
    82	    refine ⟨g, hg, ?_⟩
    83	    intro g' hg'
    84	    exact factor_through_snd_unique x₀ f hg' hg

    86	/-- The group-valued functor of points of a group object. -/
    87	abbrev pointsFunctor (G : C) [GrpObj G] : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat :=
    88	  CategoryTheory.yonedaGrpObj G
    89	
    90	/-- The functor of points is represented by the underlying group object. -/
    91	def pointsFunctor_representable (G : C) [GrpObj G] :
    92	    (pointsFunctor G ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy G :=
    93	  CategoryTheory.yonedaGrpObjRepresentableBy G

    96	   faithful.  Keeping this bundled form avoids repeatedly unpacking the
    97	   representability witness in later morphism arguments. -/
    98	def pointsYoneda : Grp C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat :=
    99	  CategoryTheory.yonedaGrp

   101	def pointsYoneda_fullyFaithful : (pointsYoneda (C := C)).FullyFaithful :=
   102	  CategoryTheory.yonedaGrpFullyFaithful

   104	theorem comp_mulRight_hom (f : X ⟶ G) (g : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   105	    f ≫ (GrpObj.mulRight g).hom = f * (toUnit X ≫ g) := by
   106	  rw [GrpObj.mulRight_hom, comp_lift_assoc, Category.comp_id,
   107	    comp_toUnit_assoc, CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
   108	
   109	theorem comp_mulRight_inv (f : X ⟶ G) (g : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   110	    f ≫ (GrpObj.mulRight g).inv = f * (toUnit X ≫ g)⁻¹ := by
   111	  rw [GrpObj.mulRight_inv, comp_lift_assoc, Category.comp_id,
   112	    ← Category.assoc, comp_toUnit, CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def,
   113	    CategoryTheory.Hom.inv_def, Category.assoc]
   114	
   115	/-- The translation carrying the section `x` to the section `y`. -/
   116	def pointTranslation (G : C) [GrpObj G] (x y : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) : G ≅ G :=
   117	  (GrpObj.mulRight x).symm ≪≫ GrpObj.mulRight y
   118	
   119	@[simp]
   120	theorem pointTranslation_self (x : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   121	    pointTranslation G x x = Iso.refl G := by
   122	  simp [pointTranslation]
   123	
   124	@[simp]
   125	theorem pointTranslation_symm (x y : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   126	    (pointTranslation G x y).symm = pointTranslation G y x := by
   127	  simp [pointTranslation]
   128	
   129	@[simp]
   130	theorem pointTranslation_trans (x y z : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   131	    pointTranslation G x y ≪≫ pointTranslation G y z = pointTranslation G x z := by
   132	  simp [pointTranslation, Iso.trans_assoc]
   133	
   134	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   135	theorem comp_pointTranslation_hom (x y : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   136	    x ≫ (pointTranslation G x y).hom = y := by
   137	  rw [pointTranslation, Iso.trans_hom, Iso.symm_hom, ← Category.assoc,
   138	    comp_mulRight_inv, comp_mulRight_hom, toUnit_unit,
   139	    Category.id_comp, Category.id_comp, mul_inv_cancel, _root_.one_mul]
   140	
   141	/- The inverse translation carries `y` back to `x`; keeping this as a named
   142	   simp lemma avoids repeating the symmetry rewrite at geometric use sites. -/
   143	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   144	theorem comp_pointTranslation_inv (x y : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   145	    y ≫ (pointTranslation G x y).inv = x := by
   146	  exact comp_pointTranslation_hom (G := G) y x
   147	
   148	/- Translation is natural for homomorphisms of group objects.  This is the
   149	   categorical transport used when moving a local fibre calculation to a
   150	   different section. -/
   151	theorem pointTranslation_hom_naturality
   152	    {G H : C} [GrpObj G] [GrpObj H]
   153	    (f : G ⟶ H) [IsMonHom f]
   154	    (x y : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   155	    (pointTranslation G x y).hom ≫ f =
   156	      f ≫ (pointTranslation H (x ≫ f) (y ≫ f)).hom := by
   157	  have hhom (g : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   158	      (GrpObj.mulRight g).hom ≫ f =
   159	        f ≫ (GrpObj.mulRight (g ≫ f)).hom := by
   160	    rw [GrpObj.mulRight_hom, Category.assoc, IsMonHom.mul_hom,
   161	      ← Category.assoc, CartesianMonoidalCategory.lift_map]
   162	    rw [GrpObj.mulRight_hom, comp_lift_assoc]
   163	    simp
   164	  have hinv (g : 𝟙_ C ⟶ G) :
   165	      (GrpObj.mulRight g).inv ≫ f =
   166	        f ≫ (GrpObj.mulRight (g ≫ f)).inv := by
   167	    rw [GrpObj.mulRight_inv, Category.assoc, IsMonHom.mul_hom,
   168	      ← Category.assoc, CartesianMonoidalCategory.lift_map]
   169	    rw [GrpObj.mulRight_inv, comp_lift_assoc]
   170	    simp
   171	  simp only [pointTranslation, Iso.trans_hom, Iso.symm_hom]
   172	  rw [Category.assoc, hhom y]
   173	  conv_lhs => rw [← Category.assoc]
   174	  rw [hinv x]
   175	  simp only [Category.assoc]

   185	/- Geometric integrality of both factors gives the integral source needed by
   186	   the rigidity argument.  The tensor object is definitionally the scheme
   187	   pullback, so the standard pullback instance applies once the first factor's
   188	   integrality and local noetherianity have been exposed. -/
   189	theorem isIntegral_tensorObj_left_of_geometricallyIntegral
   190	    {X Y : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
   191	    [GeometricallyIntegral X.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral Y.hom]
   192	    [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] :
   193	    IsIntegral (X ⊗ Y).left := by
   194	  have hX : IsIntegral X.left :=
   195	    GeometricallyIntegral.isIntegral_of_subsingleton X.hom
   196	  have hNoeth : IsLocallyNoetherian X.left :=
   197	    LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian X.hom
   198	  exact inferInstanceAs (IsIntegral (pullback X.hom Y.hom))
   199	
   200	/-- Properness of the first factor makes the second projection a closed map.
   201	
   202	The underlying scheme morphism is the pullback of `X.hom` along `Y.hom`; this
   203	is the geometric input used in the closed-map proof of the rigidity lemma. -/
   204	theorem snd_left_isClosedMap
   205	    {X Y : Over (Spec (.of kbar))} [IsProper X.hom] :
   206	    IsClosedMap (snd X Y).left.base := by
   207	  haveI hp : UniversallyClosed X.hom := IsProper.toUniversallyClosed
   208	  haveI : UniversallyClosed (snd X Y).left := by
   209	    rw [Over.snd_left]
   210	    exact universallyClosed_isStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback
   211	      (IsPullback.of_hasPullback X.hom Y.hom) hp
   212	  exact Scheme.Hom.isClosedMap _

   218	variable {W Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced W] [JacobsonSpace W] [Z.IsSeparated]
   219	
   220	/-- Two morphisms from a reduced Jacobson scheme into a separated scheme are
   221	equal when their residue-field probes agree at every closed point. -/
   222	theorem morphism_eq_of_eqAt_closedPoints
   223	    {g₁ g₂ : W ⟶ Z}
   224	    (h : ∀ x ∈ closedPoints W,
   225	      W.fromSpecResidueField x ≫ g₁ = W.fromSpecResidueField x ≫ g₂) :
   226	    g₁ = g₂ := by
   227	  let F : closedPoints W → Scheme.{u} := fun x => Spec (W.residueField x.1)
   228	  let probe : (∐ F) ⟶ W := Sigma.desc fun x => W.fromSpecResidueField x.1
   229	  haveI : IsDominant probe := by
   230	    refine ⟨(dense_iff_closure_eq.mpr (closure_closedPoints (X := W))).mono ?_⟩
   231	    intro x hx
   232	    obtain ⟨pt⟩ : Nonempty (Spec (W.residueField x)) := inferInstance
   233	    refine ⟨(Sigma.ι F ⟨x, hx⟩).base pt, ?_⟩
   234	    have hcomp : Sigma.ι F ⟨x, hx⟩ ≫ probe = W.fromSpecResidueField x :=
   235	      Sigma.ι_desc _ _
   236	    have e1 : probe.base ((Sigma.ι F ⟨x, hx⟩).base pt) =
   237	        (W.fromSpecResidueField x).base pt := by
   238	      rw [← Scheme.Hom.comp_apply, hcomp]
   239	    rw [e1]
   240	    exact Set.eq_of_mem_singleton
   241	      (Scheme.range_fromSpecResidueField x ▸ Set.mem_range_self pt)
   242	  refine ext_of_isDominant probe (Sigma.hom_ext _ _ fun x => ?_)
   243	  rw [← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc, Sigma.ι_desc]
   244	  exact h x.1 x.2

description: Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create; per-team ownership and read-state; and message other projects or teams via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
---

The inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and
future), and other projects. Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files
by hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or
fields.

## Read

- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,
  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters
  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,
  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,
  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.
- In an agent session, an unqualified list means the **open working queue**, not
  archived history. It is ordered by attention: required protections first,
  unread/direct conversations next, then advisory items. JSON starts with an
  `attention` summary so redirecting stderr cannot erase this signal.
- `horizon inbox show <id> --json` opens exactly one item and marks it read for
  your team. Use `--no-mark-read` for inspection without acknowledgement.
- Every inbox command evaluates the full local working set, even when `list` is
  filtered. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale
  memories, and consumed notices. The CLI never archives automatically because
  only the working agent can decide what is resolved; that agent must make an
  explicit cleanup pass before its final report.
- Labels are the release gate. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which
  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for
  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:
  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids
  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is
  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.
- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,
  `project:<name>`, or a **direct message** to another team: `task:<id>` /
  `run:<id>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience). A conversation
  may have several recipients; start one with `horizon inbox dm <recipient>...`.
  Scope/project says what the item is about.
- Horizon reads general items, items addressed to `horizon`, items addressed
  to its project, and DMs addressed to its own task/run. It should ignore other
  projects' and other teams' addressed items.
- A conversation's participants are its recipients **and its initiator**. The
  initiator is recorded as `metadata.started_by`; replies become unread for every
  other participant, including that initiator. Participants are not ownership:
  the initiator remains responsible for deciding when the thread is finished.
- Kinds: `conversation` (a direct/group thread requiring prompt acknowledgement),
  `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),
  `protection` (standing constraint / soft freeze), `info` (a notice for the
  human — something you did or noticed they should know, e.g. a renamed project
  or an important change; purely informational, never affects what runs),
  `memory` (durable agent note or dead end).

## Ownership & read-state (your team's inbox)

Each running session is a **team**, and the inbox is shared across teams. Two
lightweight overlays keep it navigable:

- **Ownership** — an item is either *shared with everyone* (the default) or
  *owned by one task* (that team's private inbox — e.g. its own memory). Read your
  team's inbox with `horizon inbox list --mine` (owned-by-you **plus** shared);
  another team's private items don't appear. Own an item to your task with
  `horizon inbox add --mine …` (or `--owner <task-id>`), and `horizon inbox own

  yet; `horizon inbox read <id>` marks it read, and `horizon inbox unread <id>`

  `horizon inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue — the same signal

only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
  is *not* done.
- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
  for final validation.
- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.

## When the LSP dies on big import files

The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
proof error:

- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
  the specific module you are proving in instead.
- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

## Heavy declaration isolation (advisory)

When a narrow build times out without diagnostics or an `.olean`, it can be
useful to treat that as an elaboration-localization problem rather than as a
proof failure. One possible probe is an **in-place** edit of the working Lean
file, after recording the current diff or rejected attempt so it can be
restored. Where the declaration signature can remain intact, preserve the
original proof as a clearly delimited comment and activate a typed `by sorry`
in its place. A bounded build with that stub can distinguish an expensive proof
body from a costly declaration type, imports, implicit arguments, or dependent
instances. If consumers fail after the stub builds, the exposed interface may
be insufficient.

For a useful bisection, consider progressively uncommenting or de-sorrying one
proof segment, field, map, or equality at a time in the same file, checking the
smallest faithful target after each change. Temporary `sorry`/axiom edits are
diagnostic evidence only; record them as rejected attempts and restore clean
accepted source. A clean configured build and axiom audit are useful final
evidence before accepting a result.

name: hgraph
description: The dependency graph — Horizon's vendored hgraph core keeps one file per statement/Lean declaration under <project>/hgraph/; `horizon graph frontier` ranks work and agents attach node-scoped comments and reviews. This is the only DAG engine.
---

Each project may carry an **hgraph**: a plain-files semantic graph under
`<project>/hgraph/` — one Markdown node per blueprint statement and per Lean
declaration, typed edges (`uses` = the hard dependency DAG, `formalizes` =
informal↔formal identity). `horizon graph sync` (run automatically at run boundaries)
reconciles the blueprint + Lean sources into it; your **authored** additions
(comments, reviews, metadata) are never touched by sync. The files are
committed to the workspace ledger like everything else.

Use `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …`; when a workspace has one project,
`-p` is optional. Address nodes by `label:<latex-label>` or
`decl:<lean-fqname>` — raw ids are opaque hashes. Most commands accept `--json`.

## Sync it yourself — and act on the warnings

Don't wait for the run boundary: after you change blueprint statements,
`\uses{}`/`\lean{}` annotations, or Lean declarations, run
`"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> sync` and **read its output**. Sync prints warnings for exactly the defects
you can fix on the spot: `\uses{X} has no blueprint node` (missing/mistyped
label), `\lean{Name} not found in Lean sources` (renamed or unwritten
declaration), stale nodes whose source vanished. Fix what your change caused
before moving on; a warning you deliberately leave (e.g. a forward reference
you'll write next) gets a node comment or a memory item so the next session
knows it's intentional. Sync is idempotent and never touches your authored
comments/reviews/metadata.

## Read

- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> list --state ready` — nodes whose dependencies are all closed:
  provable *now*. Other states: `closed`, `blocked`, `formalized_open`.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` — the ready nodes ranked by how many downstream nodes a
  proof would unlock. **Use this when picking the next node to prove.**
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:thm:foo` — one node: statement, `lean_status`
  (`lean_ok | mathlib_ok | sorry | empty`, derived from scanning the Lean, not
  from `\leanok`), deps, attached comments/reviews.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> ancestors label:thm:foo` — the dependency cone.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> stats` — per-state counts for the project.

## Write — per-node progress lives WITH the node

- **Comment = failure memory / progress note on that node.** When an approach
  fails or you learn something node-specific, record it where the next session
  will look first:
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> add comment label:thm:foo --content "tried simp+ring, fails because …"`
  Agent authorship plus run/session/task provenance are filled from the run
  environment; do not copy the note into the blueprint.
- **Review = a Maths / Lean verdict** (independent axes, `good|bad`):
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> add review label:thm:foo --maths good --lean bad --lean-comment "statement ok; proof has a sorry at the succ case"`
- **Metadata**: `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> modify node label:thm:foo --set status=verified`

Prefer node comments over inbox items for anything scoped to ONE node; use the
inbox (skill: `horizon-inbox`) for cross-node or cross-session coordination.

An edge `source --uses--> target` means *source depends on target*. A node is
"ready" when all of its dependencies are closed; prefer `frontier`, which ranks
ready nodes by what they unlock. The dashboard provides the workspace project
switcher and the chapter-collapsed Graphviz view.

## Relation to the blueprint

The DAG **is** the hgraph — there is no second engine and no parser fallback.
It is generated by resolving the blueprint's `\uses{}`/`\lean{}` annotations
against the real Lean sources, so keeping those annotations correct (skill:
`blueprint-conventions`) is exactly what keeps this graph correct. Unresolved
references surface as `horizon graph sync` warnings and as `dangling` entries — read
the warnings rather than trusting `dangling` alone.

name: mathlib-conventions
description: Mathlib house style for the Lean you write — naming (snake_case props / UpperCamelCase types / lowerCamelCase defs, Is-prefix, le/lt), meaningful discoverable names, preferred abstractions, and how to add a missing lemma as reusable infrastructure instead of a local hack.
---

Write Lean that looks like it belongs in mathlib: discoverable, reusable, and
composing with the existing API. This is the style side; use [[leansearch]] to
*find* lemmas and [[lean-check]] to verify, and keep the blueprint in step via
[[blueprint-conventions]].

## Naming

- **Theorems / lemmas / `Prop`s → `snake_case`**, named by *what the statement
  says*, composing the pieces in order: `add_comm`, `mul_le_mul_left`,
  `isOpen_iUnion`, `continuous_id`. A reader should reconstruct the statement
  from the name.
- **Types, structures, classes, inductives → `UpperCamelCase`**: `LinearMap`,
  `IsLindelof`, `RiemannianMetric`.
- **Definitions / terms / functions → `lowerCamelCase`**: `leviCivita`,
  `koszulRHS`, `parallelTransport`.
- **Structural predicates take the `Is` prefix**: `IsOpen`, `IsCompact`,
  `IsSymmetric`.
- **Name order relations by the operator you wrote**, not its mirror: use `le`
  / `lt` (`le_of_lt`, `add_lt_add`), not `ge` / `gt`.
- **Meaningful names only.** No `helper1`, `foo_aux`, `my_lemma`, `lemma2`.
  Ad-hoc names are invisible to search and un-reusable — the whole point of a
  mathlib-style name is that the next session (or mathlib itself) can find it.

## Search before you prove, prefer before you build

- Your "obvious lemma" is very likely already in mathlib under a more general
  name. Search first ([[leansearch]]); a negative result after a precise query
  means it's genuinely absent — then prove it, don't keep rephrasing.
- **Choose the reusable abstraction**, so your work composes with mathlib rather
  than sitting in a private silo: `Filter`/`Tendsto` over hand-rolled ε–δ, the
  Bochner `MeasureTheory.integral` over an ad-hoc integral, bundled morphisms
  (`…Hom`) and typeclasses over unbundled functions-plus-hypotheses, unless the
  problem is genuinely about the lower-level object.

## Missing infrastructure → build it properly, don't defer or hack

When a needed fact truly isn't in mathlib, the failure mode is to leave a
`sorry` "waiting for an upstream PR", or to inline a brittle one-off. Instead:

- **State the missing lemma in mathlib-ready generality**, with a proper name and
  a *real* proof attempt (a partial proof beats a documented gap), as
  project-local infrastructure others can reuse.
- **Factor hard steps into their own named, reusable lemmas** rather than a
  monolithic proof — mirroring the blueprint's "split, don't abbreviate" rule.
- **Record it** so it isn't an invisible dependency: give the new declaration a
  blueprint node (`\lean{…}` + `\uses{…}`) and note it for the roadmap, so future
  sessions and the DAG can see the new frontier ([[blueprint-conventions]], [[hgraph]]).

## House style (light touch)

- Module docstring at the top; group related material into `section`s /
  `namespace`s; keep lines readable (~100 cols); align `calc` steps.
- Prefer `simp`/`grind`-normal statements so lemmas fire as `@[simp]` candidates
  and rewrites compose.
- Comments explain the *mathematics*, not the development history ("was a sorry",
  "TODO next session" — keep that in the report/inbox, not the source).
- Mark reusable facts `@[simp]` only when they're genuinely confluent rewrites.

## Faithfulness (non-negotiable)

- **Never weaken a statement to make it pass**, and never change a declaration's
  statement to dodge its proof. A proof that games the checker is a failure.
- **No `axiom` / `admit` / `native_decide` on a goal you haven't honestly
  closed**, and no `sorry` reported as done — see [[lean-check]] for verifying a
  build is genuinely sorry-free.
